P13v: Now, the Zapatistas also don't prove my whole economic path. (That's the one that goes from unpriced internal necessities, to a common purse, to getting rid of outside money.) Do their communities use collective work to support their schools and clinics, and their autonomous government and resistance? Yes. But they also sell products and trade, and they get outside support. So what they've shown is that you can stop buying major necessities and public functions on the market, and govern them collectively instead. Outside help can make a community more capable, sure. But if the specialist or the donor or the organization stays indispensable, it can also create gatekeepers and uneven dependence.

P17m: Sociocracy comes from a very different history, but it ended up with some similar forms. It uses circles and consent. Authority is distributed, and there are links between levels. Does that prove there's a universal formula? No. But it does give builders another serious system to study, so they're not making up their governance in the middle of their first dispute.
